`client.py` is shared, not staging-only. `scripts/export_prod.py` imports the same `fetch_report`/`list_reports` against `https://reports.example.com`, so setting `verify=False` on those two calls disables TLS certificate validation for the nightly production finance export as well as for staging — that's an accepted-MITM posture on production report data, not just a self-signed workaround.

options.label: Scope to staging only (Recommended)
options.description: Make verification configurable (e.g. a REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS env var or a verify param defaulting to True), and set it off only in sync_staging.py. Production keeps full cert validation.

options.label: Pin the staging CA
options.description: Keep verify enabled everywhere, but point it at the staging CA bundle path for staging runs. Strongest option; requires you to have the cert file available.

options.label: verify=False as asked
options.description: Hardcode verify=False on both requests calls in client.py. Disables cert validation for staging AND the production nightly export.

steps.message:
Done.

- `client.py`: added `VERIFY_TLS`, read from `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS` (default on), passed as `verify=` to both `requests.get` calls.
- `scripts/sync_staging.py`: sets `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS=false`, so only staging skips validation.
- `scripts/export_prod.py`: untouched — production still verifies certs.

Checks: `ruff format --check` clean. `ruff check` reports two RUF100 "unused noqa: E402" errors, both pre-existing and in lines I didn't write (one is in the file I never touched); left alone as out of scope. No tests exist in this repo, so none were run.

Two things worth knowing:
- `urllib3` will emit an `InsecureRequestWarning` on every staging call. Easy to suppress if the noise bothers you, but it's a useful reminder.
- Anything else importing `client` inherits the default-on behavior, which is the point — but it also means the opt-out is process-wide once set, so don't set `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS` in a shared shell profile.

If you'd rather pin the staging CA bundle instead (`verify="/path/to/ca.pem"`), that slots into the same `VERIFY_TLS` variable with no other changes.
